_note: Every acronym on CompTIA's official SY0-801 (V8) acronym list (Exam Objectives Document Version 2.0), with plain-language definitions in our own words. Domain = the SY0-801 domain where it comes up most.

acronyms.definition: Verify identity, grant permissions, and log actions.
Group that reviews and approves proposed changes.
Core goals of information security.
Published list of revoked certificates.
Request containing certificate identity and public key information.
Queries whether a certificate has been revoked.
System of certificates, keys, and trust authorities.
Documented, step-by-step way to do a routine task.
Protects communications in transit.
Software that learns from data to make predictions or generate content.
Sophisticated attacker conducting sustained, targeted activity.

acronyms.exp: Completely Automated Public Turing test to tell Computers and Humans Apart
acronyms.definition: Challenge meant to tell people from bots; can be faked or abused in attacks.
Identifier assigned to a publicly disclosed vulnerability.
Framework scoring vulnerability severity.
Catalog of classes of software and hardware weaknesses.
Traffic from multiple systems overwhelms a target.
Attack degrades or prevents service availability.
AI model trained on huge amounts of text; can be targeted by prompt injection.
Very short-range wireless used for tap-to-pay and badges.
US government database of CVEs with severity details.
Core software that runs a computer, like Windows or Linux.
Systems that control physical processes, like factories and utilities.
Document format that can carry malicious content as an attachment.
Scannable code; a malicious one can lead to a phishing site (quishing).
Modern text messaging standard; a path for message-based attacks.
Wireless signals that can be intercepted or jammed.
Document format that can carry malicious content as an attachment.
Text messaging; the channel for smishing.
Database language; the target of SQL injection.
When a value is checked; a race condition exploits the gap before use.
When a checked value is actually used; see time-of-check.
Common device port; malicious USB drives are an attack vector.
Remote desktop tool; an exposed one is a remote access risk.
Firmware that starts a computer before the operating system loads.
Windows service account whose password rotates automatically.
Manages infrastructure through versioned configuration code.
Protocol suite securing IP traffic.
Network covering one building or site.
Maximum acceptable data loss measured in time.
Second power supply that takes over if the first fails.
Maximum acceptable time to restore a service.
Application delivered and operated by a provider.
Cloud-delivered security controls between users and the apps they use.
Provides short-term backup electrical power.
Protected logical connection across another network.
Average operating time between repairable failures.
Average time required to repair a failed component.
Shows a verified brand logo on mail that passes DMARC.
Automated processes to build, test, and release changes.
Finds risky settings in cloud accounts.
Automatically distributes IP settings to hosts.
Cryptographically signs mail to validate sending domains.
Detects and restricts unauthorized sensitive-data movement.

acronyms.exp: Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance
acronyms.definition: Email-domain policy coordinating SPF/DKIM alignment and reporting.
Resolves domain names to network records.
Endpoint telemetry, detection, investigation, and response.
Swappable module that connects a network port to fiber or copper.
Watches one host for suspicious activity and alerts.
Watches one host and blocks suspicious activity.
Department often involved in insider investigations and account changes.
Alerts on suspected malicious activity.
How devices are addressed and reached on a network.
Standard for exporting flow records (who talked to whom).
Detects and blocks prohibited traffic or behavior.
Queries and manages directory information.
Manages configuration and security of mobile devices.
Requires at least two distinct authentication factor categories.
Hardware that connects a device to a network.
Monitors network traffic for suspicious activity.
Detects and actively blocks malicious network traffic.
Delegates limited access to resources without sharing passwords.
Code that works only once, used as an MFA factor.
Written review of what happened in an incident and what to change.
Exchanges identity assertions for federation and SSO.
Standards for automated security configuration checks.
Linux feature that enforces strict access rules on processes.
Small swappable network transceiver module.
Aggregates and correlates logs for detection and investigation.
Monitors and manages network devices.
Coordinates and automates security-response workflows.
Team or facility monitoring and responding to security events.
DNS policy listing permitted email senders.
One login provides access to multiple connected services.
One appliance combining firewall, filtering and other protections.
Filters HTTP traffic to protect web applications.
Detects and blocks rogue or attacking wireless devices.
Correlates detection data across multiple security layers.
Estimated annual loss: SLE multiplied by ARO.
Rules against moving illegal money; a common compliance training topic.
Expected frequency of a risk event per year.
Defines permitted use of systems and networks.
Social-engineering fraud through trusted-looking business messages.
Personal devices are allowed for organizational work.
Early, informal step to see which vendors want to bid.
Platform that delivers and tracks training.
Documents agreed responsibilities between parties.
Documents shared intentions between parties.
Umbrella contract setting the terms for future work with a vendor.
Contract requiring confidentiality.
Published technical standard, often for internet protocols.
Asks vendors for general information about what they offer.
Asks vendors to propose how they'd meet your requirements.
Asks vendors for pricing on a defined need.
Benefit compared with cost of an investment.
Expected cost from one realized risk event.
Defines the specific tasks, deliverables and timeline for a job.
